collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing every laureate of the six Nobel Prize categories (Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, Peace, Economic Sciences) for prize-years 2020 through 2024 inclusive, as reported on the six per-category Wikipedia 'List of Nobel laureates in [X]' pages. The row set is what the cited Wikipedia list pages report; it is not a parametric reconstruction of Nobel Prize history. Each row contributes a (Category, Year, Laureate) triple plus the laureate's country and the verbatim citation phrase associated with the award.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics): universe + value (universe of Physics laureates 2020-2024; values for Country and Citation)
- source_urls[1] (List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Chemistry): universe + value (Chemistry laureates 2020-2024; Nationality column normalized to Country; Rationale column used as Citation)
- source_urls[2] (List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physiology_or_Medicine): universe + value (Medicine laureates 2020-2024; Nationality column used as Country; Rationale used as Citation)
- source_urls[3] (List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Literature): universe + value (Literature laureates 2020-2024; Country and Citation columns)
- source_urls[4] (List_of_Nobel_Peace_Prize_laureates): universe + value (Peace laureates 2020-2024; Country and Rationale columns; includes organization laureates)
- source_urls[5] (List_of_Nobel_Memorial_Prize_laureates_in_Economics): universe + value (Economic Sciences laureates 2020-2024; Country and Rationale columns)

Each list page is the single authoritative source for its category-partition; there is no cross-category overlap and no need for a separate validation source. The Nobel Foundation's own per-year summary pages were spot-checked against Wikipedia's Citation cells for 2020-2024 and matched verbatim modulo trailing reference-marker brackets and leading/trailing quotation marks, which were stripped during normalization.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Universe (six Nobel Prize categories), partition rule (prize-year window 2020-2024), and ranking rule (recency) are all source-defined; table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff; row count (62) is well within bounds; confidence gradient is real (Literature/Peace laureates are very memorable, while which institutional country a Chemistry laureate is attributed to is a calibration test).
- Seed/provenance: seed #23 verbatim ('For each Nobel Prize category, list the last 5 laureates with their country of affiliation, institution, and the work they were recognized for'), with two documented adaptations (see below).
- Category: multi_attribute_projection (gap 5, the largest among primary multi-source categories) with secondary temporal (the 'last 5' wording introduces a recency window).
- Source plan: six per-category Wikipedia laureate list pages; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 6.
- Expected shape: 62 rows x 5 columns; composite PK (Category, Year, Laureate).
- Domain: Science/Academia (already at one instance; this strengthens it without saturating, and the three organization Peace laureates broaden the entity-type coverage of the family).
- Risks/adaptation: 'last 5 laureates' is genuinely ambiguous (5 prize-years vs. 5 individuals); this instance picks 5 prize-years to avoid arbitrary intra-year tie-breaking. The seed's third attribute (Institution) was dropped from v1 because only the Economics list page has a structured Institution column; documented below as a known gap.
- Decision: Stage.

Deviations from picker-guide order: the recommended-next sequence in instance_selection_priorities.md (snapshot 2026-04-28) lists seed #19 ('5 most influential scientists per discipline') ahead of seed #23. Seed #19 was deferred because its universe is not source-defined (no authoritative Wikipedia/Wikidata 'top 5 by influence' ranking exists per discipline) and it would resolve as candidate_rebuild rather than source_defined. Seed #23 also fills the larger category gap.

Seed adaptations:
1. 'Last 5 laureates' -> 'all laureates from prize-years 2020-2024'. The natural alternative ('5 most recent individual laureates per category') would force tie-breaking inside a year for categories where multiple laureates share the prize (Physics 2020/2021/2022/2023, Chemistry 2022/2023/2024, Medicine 2020/2023/2024, Peace 2021/2022, Economics 2020/2021/2022/2024). Picking 5 prize-years lets the source's own award structure decide the row count.
2. 'Institution' column dropped. Pulling Institution would require either ~50 per-laureate Wikipedia/Nobel Foundation fetches or 30 per-year-per-category articles, both of which inflate source_count without strengthening the benchmark fit. A future supplement pass can add Institution.

Category <-> operation_type pairing: query_category=multi_attribute_projection pairs with operation_type=projection per references/artifact-contract.md, even though the instance also applies a temporal filter (year BETWEEN 2020 AND 2024). The projection structure (multi-column SELECT with category, year, laureate, country, citation) is the primary primitive being tested; the year filter is the scope-narrowing rule that defines the universe and is captured by secondary_category=temporal.

Post-audit (2026-04-30): bounded Wiki-family source discovery pass executed. The general 'List of Nobel laureates' page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates) and the per-year 'YYYY Nobel Prizes' summary pages were checked as candidate replacement or supplemental sources. They confirm the same 2020-2024 laureate universe by year/category but do not provide structured Country/Nationality or Citation columns at row granularity, so they would duplicate rather than replace the cited per-category list pages. No source addition was made; source_count remains 6.

Post-audit (2026-04-30): overlap with registered cfg.json::trial_union_3 was reviewed. That instance covers Nobel Physics, Chemistry, and Physiology or Medicine laureates 1945-2025 with Nationality only, structured as a UNION across three category-tables. This staged instance is structurally distinct on three independent axes: (a) six categories versus three (adds Literature, Peace, Economic Sciences); (b) narrower year window 2020-2024 versus 1945-2025; (c) adds the Citation column and structures the query as a per-category multi-attribute projection rather than a UNION. Same-entities-same-attributes-same-period overlap test (per curation_protocol.md duplicate-instance guidance) is not satisfied; no duplicate-table concern.

Post-audit (2026-04-30): table_title was edited from 'their officially attributed country' to 'their country' to remove the implicit Nobel-Foundation-canonical claim that the cited Wikipedia source set does not uniformly support (Physics/Literature/Peace/Economics use a 'Country' column header while Chemistry/Medicine use a 'Nationality' column header; the staged Country column is the cross-category-normalized merge of those, as recorded in normalization_decisions).
normalization_decisions: Country normalization: the Chemistry list page renders the 'Nationality' column as nationality adjectives (e.g., 'American', 'French', 'German', 'Danish', 'Russian', 'Tunisian'). These were converted to country names (United States, France, Germany, Denmark, Russia, Tunisia) so the Country column reads consistently across all six categories; the underlying fact is unchanged, only the surface form is standardized. The Physics, Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economics list pages already use country names and were used verbatim. Multi-citizenship cells are preserved as semicolon-delimited text (e.g., 'Hungary; United States' for Katalin Karikó, 'France; Tunisia; United States' for Moungi G. Bawendi). The Peace 2020 row uses 'United Nations' as the Country value (verbatim from the Wikipedia row) because the World Food Programme is a United Nations agency rather than a national entity. Laureate normalization: birth/death year parentheticals ('(b. 1968)', '(1943-2023)', '(founded 1961)') and footnote markers ('[J]', '[K]', '[D]') were stripped from Laureate, Country, and Citation cells. Laureate names are otherwise verbatim from the source page including initials and middle initials (e.g., 'John J. Hopfield', 'David W.C. MacMillan', 'K. Barry Sharpless'). Citation normalization: trailing reference-marker brackets ([124], [125], etc.) were stripped, and leading/trailing typesetting quotation marks (straight or curly) were stripped because they wrap the phrase rather than belong to it. Internal punctuation, capitalization (Physics's 'For' vs. other categories' 'for'), and trailing periods are preserved verbatim.
open_questions: 1. Whether to add an Institution / Affiliation column in a v2: the seed asks for 'institution' and the Economics list page already has it; supplementing the other five categories from per-laureate Nobel Foundation 'facts' pages would give a faithful 'institution at time of award' attribute but would push source_count to ~50+. A v2 would either accept the source-count expansion or restructure as a partially_supplemented claim with the per-laureate pages cited as entity-detail sources. 2. Whether Country should be reduced to a single canonical value per laureate (the Nobel Foundation's official primary attribution) rather than the multi-citizenship list Wikipedia uses; current rendering preserves whatever the cited list page reports, which may differ from Nobel Foundation's single-country attribution for laureates with dual citizenship. 3. Whether the Peace 2022 shared citation (which Wikipedia repeats verbatim across all three laureates: 'The Peace Prize laureates represent civil society in their home countries...') should be replaced by per-laureate paraphrases on a v2 — this would lose source verbatim grounding but improve cell-level differentiation.
